promise_quote: Understanding the birth of galaxies, stars, and planets; cycling of matter through the interstellar medium
science_question: Understand the birth of galaxies, stars, and planets through infrared observations
rationale: U.S. contribution to JAXA-ESA mission; notional budget of $150M includes operations over the decade

promise_quote: Submillimeter surveys enabling broad extragalactic, galactic, and outer-solar-system science
science_question: Conduct sensitive submillimeter surveys across cosmic time to study galaxy evolution and star formation
rationale: Total construction cost $140M; US federal share $37M (33% of total); operations $11M total, $7.5M federal share

promise_quote: Dark energy, dark matter, time-variable phenomena, supernovae, Kuiper belt and near-Earth objects
science_question: Determine the nature of dark energy and dark matter through weak gravitational lensing and supernovae surveys
rationale: Total construction cost $465M; US federal share $421M; annual operations $42M total, $28M federal share

promise_quote: Broad science; peer-reviewed program for projects that fall between the NSF MRI and MREFC limits
science_question: Enable rapid response to scientific discovery and technical advances with new telescopes and instruments
rationale: Cost range $93M to $200M; competed program; no specific technical risk rating given

promise_quote: Studies of the earliest galaxies and galactic evolution; detection and characterization of planetary systems
science_question: Study the earliest galaxies and their evolution; detect and characterize planetary systems around nearby stars
rationale: Total cost $1.1B-$1.4B (for Giant Magellan Telescope vs Thirty Meter Telescope); US federal share $257M-$350M (~25%); operations $36M-$55M total, $9M-$14M federal share

promise_quote: Indirect detection of dark matter; particle acceleration and active galactic nucleus science
science_question: Study very high energy gamma rays to detect dark matter and probe particle acceleration in active galactic nuclei
rationale: Total construction cost $400M; US federal share $100M; U.S. joins European Čerenkov Telescope Array; operations cost unknown

promise_quote: Preparation for a planet-imaging mission beyond 2020, including precursor science activities
science_question: Develop technology to image habitable rocky planets in the habitable zones of nearby stars
rationale: Notional budget $100M-$200M; early-decade activity $4M/year, late-decade mission development up to $200M mid-decade pending mid-decade review

promise_quote: Cosmic microwave background (CMB)/ inflation technology development and preparation for a possible mission beyond 2020
science_question: Develop technology to detect telltale evidence that cosmic inflation actually occurred
rationale: Notional budget range $60M-$200M for technology development; mission scope and cost beyond 2020 uncertain

promise_quote: Dark energy, exoplanets, and infrared survey-science
science_question: Why is the expansion rate of the universe accelerating and are there other solar systems like ours with worlds like Earth
rationale: Total cost $1.6B (70% confidence level); 82 months from project start to launch; based on mature technologies with relatively low technical risk

promise_quote: Enable rapid response to science opportunities; augments current plan by 2 Medium-scale Explorer (MIDEX) missions, 2 Small Explorer (SMEX) missions, and 4 Missions of Opportunity (MoOs)
science_question: Enable rapid response to new scientific discoveries through flexible, competitively-selected missions
rationale: Total decade cost $463M; increases annual astrophysics budget from ~$40M to ~$100M by 2015; includes 2 MIDEX, 2 SMEX, 4 Missions of Opportunity

promise_quote: Open low-frequency gravitational-wave window for detection of black-hole mergers and compact binaries and precision tests of general relativity
science_question: Detect gravitational waves from merging black holes and test general relativity in strong-field regimes
rationale: Total cost $2.4B (70% confidence); US share $1.5B; US 2012-2021 share $852M; requires ESA partnership (L-class mission); technical risk medium if LISA Pathfinder succeeds

promise_quote: Black-hole accretion and neutron-star physics, matter/energy life cycles, and stellar astrophysics
science_question: Understand black-hole accretion, matter cycling through galaxies, and hot gas physics with X-ray spectroscopy
rationale: Total cost $5.0B (70% confidence); US share $3.1B; US 2012-2021 share $200M; partnership with ESA and JAXA; medium-high technical risk due to large-aperture mirror challenges and immature secondary instruments
